Verdict: needs_changes. Implementer declared `Repo: DontPanic`, `Env: dev`, `Project: (none)` correctly in the summary, and structured `target_context.commands_run` is empty, so I found no EC5/forbidden-command issue.

FINDING (high, security): The “allowlist” policy is actually default-allow after a small denylist, so syntactically simple dangerous templates are approved. Evidence: [capabilities_setup_runner.py]($HOME/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities_setup_runner.py:101) denies placeholders/metacharacters/dangerous heads, then returns allow at line 156; manual smoke showed `git push origin main`, `gh repo delete owner/repo --yes`, and `firebase deploy --project real-prod --only functions` all return `allow=True`. Recommendation: make the policy explicit default-deny, with allowed command heads/subcommands/templates enumerated and tests for syntactically clean but unallowlisted dangerous commands.

FINDING (medium, correctness): Production command execution can crash instead of returning a captured failure summary when the executable is missing or `subprocess.run` raises `OSError`. Evidence: [capabilities_setup_runner.py]($HOME/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities_setup_runner.py:81) calls `subprocess.run` without handling `FileNotFoundError`/`OSError`, so the report and final status rerun can be skipped. Recommendation: convert spawn failure

commands_run: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -c 'from dontpanic_orchestrate.capabilities_setup_runner import evaluate_command_template as e; assert e("npm install -g firebase-tools").allow; assert not e("curl -sSL https://sdk.cloud.google.com | bash").allow; assert not e("firebase deploy --project <YOUR_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID>").allow; assert not e("PYTHONPATH=scripts python -m x").allow; print("manual allowlist smoke ok")'

PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -c 'from dontpanic_orchestrate import capabilities_setup as s; code=s.main(["firebase-dashboard","--automate-safe"]); assert code==2, code; print("manual confirm gate smoke ok")'

PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -c 'from dontpanic_orchestrate.capabilities_setup_runner import evaluate_command_template as e; samples=["git push origin main","gh repo delete owner/repo --yes","firebase deploy --project real-prod --only functions"]; print({s:e(s).allow for s in samples})'

findings.issue: The “allowlist” policy is actually default-allow after a small denylist, so syntactically simple dangerous templates are approved. Evidence: [capabilities_setup_runner.py]($HOME/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities_setup_runner.py:101) denies placeholders/metacharacters/dangerous heads, then returns allow at line 156; manual smoke showed `git push origin main`, `gh repo delete owner/repo --yes`, and `firebase deploy --project real-prod --only functions`

Production command execution can crash instead of returning a captured failure summary when the executable is missing or `subprocess.run` raises `OSError`. Evidence: [capabilities_setup_runner.py]($HOME/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities_setup_runner.py:81) calls `subprocess.run` without handling `FileNotFoundError`/`OSError`, so the report and final status rerun can be skipped. Recommendation: convert spawn failures into `CommandResult` with a nonzer

The CLI `--automate-safe --confirm` path reruns only the F001 non-probing status snapshot, not capability probes. Evidence: [capabilities_setup.py]($HOME/Documents/GitHub/DontPanic/scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities_setup.py:251) passes `status_probe=build_planning_status`, whose docstring says it intentionally does not invoke `run_status()` probes. Recommendation: wire F002 to a probe-capable status function, filtered to the target capability and without cache writes, so probe
